chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Dawud al-Mustarriq from Umm Saeed al-Ahmasiyyah, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I had sent someone to rent a donkey for me to go to the graves of the martyrs. He (peace be upon him) said: 'What prevents you from visiting the Chief of the Martyrs?' She said: 'I said, and who is he? May I be your ransom.' He said: 'That is al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).' She said: 'I said, and what is the reward for one who visits him?' He said: 'A Hajj and an Umrah, and from the good, so and so.' He counted three times with his hand.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, Umm Saeed al-Ahmasiyyah receives a specific directive from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) to prioritize the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.) over the general cemetery of martyrs, establishing his unique status as *Sayyid al-Shuhada* (Chief of Martyrs). The Imam’s declaration that visiting him yields the reward of a Hajj and an Umrah, repeated three times, underscores the profound spiritual merit of Ziyarat in Shia tradition, linking physical pilgrimage to divine acceptance and abundant goodness.
